# Battle of Dura-Europos

| combatant1        = Roman Empire
| combatant2        = Parthian Empire
| commander1        = Avidius Cassius
| commander2        = Unknown
| date              = 165
| units1            = Legio III Gallica
| units2            = Parthian garrison
| territory         = Romans recapture Dura-Europos.
}}
The Battle of Dura-Europos, as retold by Lucian of Samosata, was a clash between the forces of the Roman Empire commanded by Avidius Cassius against a Parthian garrison resisting the siege. The city was eventually captured and, as reported by Marcus Statius Priscus, 70,236 Parthians were slaughtered in the battle, with the romans suffering only 2 dead and 7 wounded. However, Lucian himself denies this claim. Scholar Peter Edwell noted that Lucian referred to the Europus battle on numbers of occasions and complained that a contemporary source summarised the battle in only seven lines, all of which suggests that the battle was actually significant and the casualties reported may have some true aspect in their numbers. According to Belgian historian Franz Cumont, the battle marked the Roman takeover of the city of Dura, however Peter Edwell again pointed out that Lucian was referring to another city, much further up along the Euphrates. Archeological traces along the wall defenses of the besieged city have been ascribed to a Roman assault on the city of Dura-Europus itself, ultimately confirming the location of the battle. Further archeological research showed the breached walls of the city, implying that it was taken over by the Romans. Nevertheless, after the battle, Avidius Cassius advanced as far as Ctesiphon and Seleucia. Following the war, a Roman garrison of Syrian troops was enstablished in the city. The new garrison possibly included the legions IIII Scythica and XVI Flavia Firma.
